items.title: Section: Giving Even Amid Genuine Scarcity — Better to Go Hungry Than Turn Someone Away

items.zh: 又諸菩薩若見求者正現在前，由諸財物有尠闕故，於其惠施心不趣入。菩薩爾時即以正慧速疾通達如是匱乏障施因緣，忍受匱乏所作眾苦，力勵思擇，起悲愍心而行慧施。
items.en: Bodhisattvas, seeing a petitioner genuinely present but finding their own means genuinely scarce, may find their mind reluctant to give. They swiftly recognise this scarcity itself as an obstacle to giving, resolve to bear whatever hardship results from that scarcity, and, forcing the choice through compassion, give anyway.

items.zh: 作如是念：或由宿業有過失故，或由現在繫屬他故，令我具受眾多猛利飢渴等苦，不能饒益一切眾生。
設我今者由行惠施，因饒益他，於現法中受種種苦，乃至殞歿，如是行施猶為最勝，非空發遣諸來求者；況當更有諸菜葉等可以活命。菩薩如是忍受匱乏所作眾苦而行惠施。
items.en: Even should I, by giving in order to benefit another, suffer all manner of hardship in this very life, even unto death, giving in this way is still supreme — never sending a petitioner away empty-handed — how much more so, then, when I still have even wild greens enough to sustain life. Bodhisattvas bear the hardship of genuine scarcity in just this way, and give.

items.title: Section: Cutting Attachment at Its Root — Giving Away Precisely the Most Cherished Thing

items.zh: 又諸菩薩，若見求者正現在前，由可施物極悅意故、最上妙故，於行惠施心不趣入。菩薩爾時即以正慧速疾通達，是我耽著所作過失，我今於苦發起虛妄樂想顛倒，由此能生當來眾苦。
items.en: Bodhisattvas, seeing a petitioner genuinely present but finding the object requested especially pleasing and exquisite, may find their mind reluctant to give. They swiftly recognise, through genuine wisdom, that this reluctance is the fault of their own attachment, giving rise to a distorted, false sense of pleasure in what is genuinely suffering, and that this very attachment produces further suffering to come.

items.zh: 於此顛倒遍了知故，為欲斷除，力勵思擇，用此財物而行惠施。
items.en: Fully recognising this distortion, and wishing to root it out entirely, the bodhisattva forces the choice and gives away precisely this cherished object.

items.zh: 又諸菩薩若行施已，於當施果廣大財利，見勝功德，深生欣樂，不求無上正等菩提。菩薩爾時即以正慧速疾通達，是邪果見所作過失。

items.title: Section: Seeing Through Impermanence Dissolves the Wrong View of Future Reward

items.zh: 如實觀察一切諸行皆不堅牢，一切諸行皆念念滅，所受用果速疾滅盡、速疾離散。如是觀時，即能斷滅能生欣樂邪果之見，諸所行施一切迴向無上菩提。
items.en: Truly observing that every conditioned thing is fundamentally unstable, arising and perishing moment by moment, and that whatever result is enjoyed swiftly perishes and swiftly scatters away — observing in this way, one is able to dissolve the distorted view that delights in a future reward, and dedicates all giving instead towards unsurpassed awakening.

items.title: Section: Four Antidotes Working Together, and Giving's Supreme Fruit Secured

items.zh: 如是菩薩四種施障，當知四種能對治智對治於彼。一者、覺悟，二者、忍受眾苦，三者、遍知顛倒，四者、見一切行性不堅牢。
items.en: These four obstacles to a bodhisattva's giving are each met by their own antidote of understanding: first, awareness; second, willingness to bear hardship; third, full recognition of distortion; fourth, seeing that all conditioned things are fundamentally unstable.

items.zh: 是諸菩薩由前三種能對治智，決定堪能正行惠施；由後一種能對治智，能正攝受施福勝果。
items.en: Bodhisattvas, through the first three antidotes, become genuinely capable of correctly practising giving; through the fourth antidote alone, they rightly secure giving's own supreme, resulting fruit.

items.zh: 當知亦名菩薩巧慧而行布施。

items.title: Section: Giving Through Meditative Mastery — Manifesting Inexhaustible Treasures

items.zh: 又諸菩薩內居閑靜，由淨意樂淳厚淨信分別勝解，數數緣念種種上妙無量財寶，以勝解力，於諸眾生樂行惠施。由此因緣，是諸菩薩以少功用生無量福，當知亦名菩薩巧慧而行布施。
items.en: Bodhisattvas, dwelling inwardly in quiet solitude, through pure intention, deep and genuine faith, and discerning conviction, repeatedly call to mind abundant, exquisite wealth of every kind, and, through the power of that conviction, delight in giving to beings. Through this, bodhisattvas generate boundless merit through remarkably little effort. This too should be understood as a bodhisattva's giving guided by skilful wisdom.

items.title: Section: Skilful Giving Concludes — Six Categories Named Together, a New Angle Opens

items.zh: 如是妙慧大慧菩薩巧慧行施總略義者，由有財、無財，財施所攝故；如是由法施故，由無礙解施故，由勝意樂施故，由施障對治智慧施故，由增上意樂勝解施故，當知是名唯諸菩薩不共行施。
items.en: The summary of a bodhisattva's giving guided by fine, expansive, skilful wisdom is this: giving from wealth or without it; giving the teaching; giving through unobstructed understanding; giving shaped by the immeasurables; giving that overcomes its own obstacles; and giving through meditative conviction. This should be understood as giving unique to bodhisattvas, shared with no one else.

items.zh: 如是廣說於內外事菩薩所行一切施差別相已。自斯已後，即於一切施差別相中，分出所餘難行施等一切差別，應當了知。
items.en: Having broadly explained the distinctions of every kind of giving a bodhisattva practices, both internal and external, from this point on, the remaining distinctions within comprehensive giving — difficult giving and the rest — should further be understood.

items.zh: 云何菩薩難行施？當知此施略有三種。
謂若諸菩薩財物尠少，自忍貧苦惠施於他，是名菩薩第一難行施。
items.en: Bodhisattvas who, having very little wealth, personally bear poverty and hardship while still giving to others — this is called a bodhisattva's first kind of difficult giving.

items.zh: 若諸菩薩所可愛物，或性深愛著，或長時串習，或有上品恩，或最上妙物，極生耽著，能自開解，惠施於他，是名菩薩第二難行施。若諸菩薩極大艱辛所獲財物惠施於他，是名菩薩第三難行施。
items.en: Bodhisattvas who, towards something genuinely cherished — deeply attached to by nature, long relied upon, owed to for great past kindness, or simply the very finest thing owned, generating real, deep attachment — are nonetheless able to let go and give it to another: this is called a bodhisattva's second kind of difficult giving. Bodhisattvas who give away wealth obtained only through extreme hardship: this is called a bodhisattva's third kind of difficult giving.

items.zh: 云何菩薩一切門施？當知此施略有四相。

items.title: Section: Giving Through Every Gateway — Four Aspects

items.zh: 謂諸菩薩，或自財物，或勸化他所得財物，或施親屬、父母、妻子、奴婢、作使、善友、大臣、親戚、眷屬，或復施與他來求者。如是四相，是名菩薩一切門施。
items.en: Bodhisattvas give from their own wealth, or from wealth gathered by persuading others; give to relatives — parents, spouse, servants, staff, close friends, ministers, kin, and household; or give to whoever comes seeking help. These four aspects are called a bodhisattva's giving through every gateway.

items.title: Section: Giving as a Genuinely Good Person Opens — Pure Faith, Respect, One's Own Hand, Right Timing

items.zh: 云何菩薩善士所行名善士施？當知此施略有五相。謂諸菩薩，淨信而施，恭敬而施，自手而施，應時而施，
items.en: What is called giving as a genuinely good person? This giving should be understood as, in brief, five marks. Bodhisattvas give from pure faith, give with respect, give with their own hand, and give at the right time.

blocks.text: How each obstacle to giving is overcome, and further aspects of giving.

Finding means scarce, "they resolve to bear whatever hardship results", reflecting: "even should I suffer, even unto death, giving in this way is still supreme: never sending a petitioner away empty-handed." Master Cháng Bǎi: one can always eat greens and wild plants.

"Finding the object especially pleasing, they recognise that this attachment is a distortion", "and give away precisely this cherished object". Master Cháng Bǎi: give the very best, cutting one's own craving.
"Seeing that every conditioned thing is unstable, arising and perishing moment by moment", they give without wishing for reward. Venerable Miào Jìng recalls how even great statesmen's power vanished.
Awareness, bearing hardship, recognising distortion, and seeing impermanence. "Through the first three, one practises giving correctly; through the fourth, one secures its supreme fruit."
Bodhisattvas with meditative mastery call to mind abundant wealth and, through concentration, make it appear to give.

Three kinds: giving while poor oneself; giving what one cherishes most ("long relied upon, owed for great past kindness, or simply the finest thing one owns"); and giving "wealth obtained only through extreme hardship".

subs.head: Every gateway; a good person's giving

blocks.text: From one's own wealth or by persuading others; to relatives, to strangers, to anyone. A good person gives "from pure faith, with respect, with their own hand, at the right time", and "without causing distress to others". Master Cháng Bǎi: if one's own family is distressed by the giving, something is wrong.

quiz.q: A petitioner is present, but the bodhisattva's means are scarce and the mind is reluctant. How does the treatise say the bodhisattva overcomes this?
options: bear the hardship of scarcity, force the choice, and give out of compassion
tell the petitioner one is also poor
quiz.why: They recognise scarcity as an obstacle, "resolve to bear whatever hardship results from that scarcity, and, forcing the choice through compassion, give anyway." Master Cháng Bǎi: even though giving leaves oneself with nothing, one still gives.

quiz.q: "How much more so, then, when I still have even wild greens enough to sustain life." What does Master Cháng Bǎi say?
options: besides, one still has greens — sweet-potato leaves and wild grasses are enough to live on
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: besides, one still has greens — sweet-potato leaves, wild grasses, and the like are enough to live on. Venerable Miào Jìng: I still have a mouthful of rice; I won't die right away.

quiz.q: When reluctant because the requested object is especially pleasing, the bodhisattva "gives away precisely this cherished object." How does Master Cháng Bǎi stress this?
options: one must give the very best item, cutting away one's own craving
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: one must give the very best item to the other person, cutting away one's own craving. All craving is suffering; all craving ends in exhaustion.

quiz.q: Each of the four obstacles has an antidote. What is the antidote to the fourth, delight in future wealth?
options: seeing that all conditioned things are fundamentally unstable
quiz.why: The four antidotes are awareness, bearing hardship, full recognition of distortion, and seeing that all conditioned things are unstable; "through the fourth antidote alone, they rightly secure giving's own supreme, resulting fruit." Venerable Miào Jìng: "secure" here means accomplish.

quiz.q: "Dwelling in quiet solitude … repeatedly calling to mind abundant wealth, and through the power of conviction, delighting in giving." What kind of bodhisattva is this, according to the lectures, and by what power?
options: an ordinary bodhisattva, through hard work
a noble bodhisattva who has entered meditative absorption, giving through mastery of concentration
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: this is a noble bodhisattva with the four absorptions and eight attainments, giving through mastery of concentration. Venerable Miào Jìng: "pure intention, deep faith, and discerning conviction" really means having entered meditative absorption.

quiz.q: What is the bodhisattva's first kind of difficult giving?
options: giving wealth won through extreme hardship
having very little, bearing poverty oneself while giving to others
quiz.why: "Bodhisattvas who, having very little wealth, personally bear poverty and hardship while still giving to others — this is called a bodhisattva's first kind of difficult giving." Master Cháng Bǎi: having no money left, yet when it is time to give, giving generously and much.

quiz.q: Of the five marks of giving as a genuinely good person, what are the first four?
options: giving from pure faith, with respect, with one's own hand, at the right time
quiz.why: "Bodhisattvas give from pure faith, give with respect, give with their own hand, and give at the right time." The fifth is giving without causing distress to another. Master Cháng Bǎi: being free of greed, hatred, and delusion is "good," and "shì" means a person.
